summary:
RotateWise is an agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into practical crop-planning insights. It integrates historical climate observations from NASA POWER with farm-specific soil information, crop history, and agronomic knowledge to help users evaluate crop suitability and design sustainable crop rotations.

Farmers can explore ten major crops, compare their climate and soil compatibility, build multi-season rotation plans, and simulate hypothetical drought, excess rainfall, temperature, and irrigation scenarios. A transparent scoring engine evaluates climate, water, soil, seasonal, and rotation compatibility while identifying risks, missing information, and data limitations.

By connecting NASA climate data with crop intelligence and interactive scenario analysis, RotateWise aims to make agricultural planning more informed, understandable, and adaptable to changing environmental conditions. It is designed to support better decisions, not replace local agricultural expertise.
details:
What is RotateWise?

RotateWise is a web-based agricultural intelligence and decision-support platform designed to help farmers make more informed crop selection and crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data and agronomic knowledge.

How it works

The platform integrates NASA POWER's historical daily Agroclimatology data through its API. It retrieves seven environmental parameters, including mean, maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation.

Users can register farm profiles with location coordinates, soil characteristics, irrigation availability, and crop history. RotateWise retrieves historical climate observations for the selected farm and combines them with a structured knowledge database covering ten crops: Rice, Wheat, Maize, Cotton, Soybean, Groundnut, Chickpea, Sorghum, Pearl Millet, and Mustard.

A deterministic crop suitability engine evaluates five dimensions: climate, water, soil, growing season, and crop rotation compatibility. Users receive transparent scores, supporting reasons, limitations, and potential cultivation risks.

The Crop Rotation Planner helps users design and compare multi-season crop sequences. It evaluates botanical crop families, nutrient management, root-depth diversity, and potential pest and disease carryover.

The Climate Scenario Simulator allows users to explore hypothetical rainfall changes, temperature shifts, irrigation strategies, and alternative crop selections. It compares simulated outcomes against historical NASA POWER baselines without presenting scenarios as actual forecasts.

Benefits and Intended Impact

RotateWise aims to make climate information more accessible and actionable for agricultural planning. It can help users:

  • Understand historical climate conditions at a selected farm location.
  • Compare crops against local climate and soil characteristics.
  • Identify potential crop rotation conflicts.
  • Explore how drought, excess rainfall, or temperature changes could affect crop suitability.
  • Understand the assumptions, risks, and limitations behind recommendations.

The intended impact is to support more climate-aware, resource-conscious, and informed agricultural decisions.

Technology and Resources

The application was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Recharts, and Lucide React. NASA POWER provides the historical meteorological data. The application uses a backend service for API integration, TypeScript-based agronomic calculation engines, and browser localStorage for farm and scenario persistence.

The interface is designed to be responsive across desktop and mobile devices.

Creativity and Innovation

RotateWise connects satellite-derived climate information, crop knowledge, crop rotation intelligence, and interactive climate scenario analysis into one integrated workflow.

Rather than presenting a recommendation as an unexplained AI-generated answer, the platform uses transparent deterministic scoring and shows the factors behind each result. Missing data and confidence limitations are explicitly communicated.

The simulator enables users to investigate hypothetical environmental changes and compare agricultural choices before making real-world decisions.

Data Integrity and Limitations

NASA POWER historical observations are distinguished from hypothetical scenario outputs and demonstration data. The platform does not claim to provide field-level crop-health detection, guaranteed yields, market prices, or financial forecasts. Its recommendations are intended as decision support and should be considered alongside local agricultural expertise.

Use of Super Intelligence

AI-assisted development tools, including ChatGPT and Google AI Studio, were used to support software development, code generation, debugging, and refinement. AI assistance was not treated as a replacement for NASA data or the deterministic agronomic scoring calculations. Any AI-assisted content, code, or media is disclosed in the appropriate project indicators.
